gloss: um; uh; let me see; well

definitions.gloss: um; uh; let me see; well
definitions.explanation: A common filler word used when pausing to think or recall something in casual conversation. Placed at the beginning of a sentence while the speaker gathers their thoughts.

examples.japanese: えっと、⟦{何|なん}→何〜：03100_nan⟧だ⟦っけ→っけ：10739_kke⟧。
えっと、⟦{次|つぎ}→次：00819_tsugi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{三時|さんじ}→三時：10983_sanji⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧です。
examples.english: Um, the next meeting is from three o'clock.

examples.japanese: えっと、⟦{確|たし}か→確か：00894_tashika⟧⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{近|ちか}くにあった⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧んだ⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧。
examples.english: Let me see... I think it was near the station.

notes:
A common filler word used when pausing to think or recall something. Very natural in casual spoken Japanese. Used at the beginning of a sentence or as a standalone hesitation.

USAGE:
Typically placed at the start of a sentence while the speaker gathers their thoughts. Common in everyday conversation. Not used in formal writing or speeches.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ええ→ええ：02893_ee⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧: a slightly longer variant with the same meaning
- ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧: um/uh — another common hesitation filler, slightly more polite
- ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧: well/um — used as a filler, often before a delicate or difficult topic
- ⟦ええ→ええ：02893_ee⟧: yes/yeah — can also function as a filler but primarily means "yes"

REGISTER:
Informal spoken language. Avoid in formal contexts, presentations, or written Japanese.
